description:
Sweep result: 1 PASS (jmap-types) / 24 FAIL. All 24 failures share one shape: `failed to select a version for the requirement <dep> = ^X.Y.Z — candidate versions found which didn't match: <older>`.

This is NOT a defect in any Cargo.toml. It's the chicken-and-egg of a multi-crate workspace bumping shared types ahead of publishing. Once each layer is published in topological order, the next layer's dry-run will succeed.

Recommended publish ordering (verified against actual dep graph):

1. jmap-types 0.1.1 (already passes dry-run)
2. (parallel) jmap-mail-types 0.1.1, jmap-chat-types 0.1.1, jmap-contacts-types 0.1.1, jmap-calendars-types 0.1.1, jmap-tasks-types 0.1.1, jmap-filenode-types 0.1.1, jmap-sharing-types 0.1.1
3. jmap-mime 0.1.1
4. jmap-server 0.1.2
5. jmap-base-client 0.1.1
6. (parallel) all 7 *-server and 7 *-client crates

Each step requires registry indexing of the previous step (a few seconds typically).

Action: document this ordering in a top-level RELEASING.md or in CONTRIBUTING.md so the next person to do a release doesn't have to rediscover it.

P3 because not a code defect — it's documentation of process. Convergence eligible.
notes:
Documented in RELEASING.md (commit 8f5014e). Covers:
- Why ordering matters (cargo strips path on publish)
- Dependency graph as a 7-layer topological order
- Per-layer publish procedure (parallelism within a layer is safe)
- Pre-publish checklist (fmt/clippy/test/doc)
- Version bump conventions (workspace 0.1.X line, propagation rule reminder)
- Tracking (when to update this file)

Verified the bead's stated layer ordering against actual Cargo.toml dep edges:
- jmap-types: no jmap deps (layer 1)
- jmap-{ext}-types: depend on jmap-types only (layer 2, parallel)
- jmap-mime: depends on jmap-types + jmap-mail-types (layer 3)
- jmap-server: depends on jmap-types only (layer 4, parallel with layer 5)
- jmap-base-client: depends on jmap-types only (layer 5, parallel with layer 4)
- jmap-mail-server: depends on jmap-types + jmap-mail-types + jmap-server + jmap-mime (layer 6)
- jmap-{ext}-server (×6): depends on jmap-types + jmap-{ext}-types + jmap-server (layer 6, parallel)
- jmap-{ext}-client (×7): depends on jmap-types + jmap-{ext}-types + jmap-base-client (layer 7, parallel)

Differs slightly from bead text — bead said jmap-mime in step 3 with jmap-mail-types as prereq, which is correct. Bead also clusters server+client into layer 6, but they actually split (server depends on jmap-mime+jmap-server, client depends on jmap-base-client). Documented as layers 6 (server) and 7 (client) for clarity.
title: P3: cargo publish --dry-run fails for 24 of 25 crates due to unpublished bumped versions
